$comment: Brand settings for Tailzu. Edit, then run `npm run build`. Choices echo the brand's own signals (identity.json -> signals).
name: Tailzu

color.$comment: Palettes by combination number (1-348) from Sanzo Wada's A Dictionary of Color Combinations; browse them in the brand hub (Colour tab). "primary" is the default (--<prefix>-bg, -ink, -accent ...). mode "light" puts the lightest colour in the background, "dark" the darkest. status: "placeholder" until the owner agrees, then "chosen".

typography.$comment: A pairing id from foundations/typography/source/pairings.json; compare them in the brand hub (Typography tab). scale is the ratio between type sizes. hand is one handwritten accent face from foundations/typography/source/handwritten.json, allowed by the style (approaches/humanist-minimal/typography.json -> handwritten: accent, one note of six words or fewer per piece).

$why.approach: Humanist Minimal (evidence 12/14, the highest in the guide): its method is the brand's own idea. The site's README says 'Speech is a person, and a person writes by hand ... Hand in, type out: that contrast is the product'. In this style the hand lives in the ink line and one short note, and the type stays calm: the said line is the hand, the written line is the type.
$why.primary: Wada 126 in dark mode (Deep Lyons Blue ground, Ivory Buff text 6.61:1, Yellow Ocher accent 5.02:1): the og.png card in Wada's colours, an indigo-blue night, cream words and one amber object (the full stop that lands last).
$why.night: Wada 232 in dark mode (Deep Indigo ground, Pinkish Cinnamon text 10.1:1, Carmine accent): the deepest indigo in the book, nearest to the og.png ground #17163F, with the site's rose as the one accent object. Also a style-recommended combination (art.json).
$why.desk: Wada 190 in dark mode (Black ground, Ivory Buff text 12.75:1, English Red accent 5.22:1): the app's own near-black ground #0F0D0B with the mark's cream line and copper tail. For the desktop and code-editor pieces.
$why.paper: Wada 151 in light mode (Sulpher Yellow ground, Vandar Poel's Blue text 7.51:1, Yellow Orange accent): the site's paper and butter sections with its saffron, for longer copy that must be dark on light (O8) and for professional pieces.
$why.pairing: instrument (Instrument Serif + Instrument Sans + IBM Plex Mono), rated core by the style: two of its three faces are the site's own (Instrument Sans, IBM Plex Mono); Instrument Serif is the pairing's nearest light editorial serif to the site's Newsreader.
$why.hand: Caveat: the site's own face for the spoken word. Handwriting research: hand type makes people feel a person was there (Schroll et al. 2018), so it carries the said line; machine type is read as clearer and more credible (Song & Schwarz 2008; Song et al. 2025), so the written line, names and numbers stay in the pairing. One note of six words or fewer per piece, never a headline, CTA or number.
